objective.name: find_within.py
objective.purpose: Read a targeted window/region of a file by pattern instead of a grep|cut|sed pipeline. Three modes: (1) a pattern match with N lines of context (-A/-B/-C), (2) a trailing/leading window from a match, (3) the inclusive region between two patterns (--between). With no flags it prints every match with line numbers to stdout. Backs the find-within skill.
objective.side_effects: Read-only. Reads the named file(s), prints sliced output (line-numbered) to stdout; non-fatal per-file errors go to stderr. No files written.
path_assumptions: Path args may be globs; glob expansion applies
Reads from cwd or absolute paths; no cwd assumption

switches.effect: Region mode: print from each match of PATTERN to the next match of ENDPAT, inclusive. Last positional becomes the file/glob.
Lines of trailing context after a match
Lines of leading context before a match
Treat patterns as literal strings (re.escape), not regex
Only the first match/region, then exit
Only the last match (single-pattern mode; ignored with --between)
Print only the total match count across all files, then exit

objective.required_arguments: PATTERN and at least one PATH (file or glob)
objective.explicit_env_checks: false — no environment to check; argparse validates flags and reports regex errors clearly

subjective.usual_invocation: Invoked indirectly by the find-within skill on the developer's behalf to read a slice of a file with fewer tokens than a grep pipeline; occasionally run directly by a developer at the CLI.
subjective.invocation_change_recommendation: None. argparse switch-form is already idiomatic and grep-compatible (-A/-B/-C/-i/-F). No verb form, no 'python3 < file' pattern.
subjective.linux_changes_needed: None. Pure stdlib, no OS-specific calls. Runs unchanged in an Ubuntu container.
subjective.typical_runtime: Sub-second for typical source files; single pass over lines.
subjective.slow_switch_warning: None. No switch exceeds 2 minutes. Reads the whole file into memory, so a multi-GB file would be slow/memory-heavy — not a normal case.
subjective.dry_run_recommendation: Not applicable — the tool is read-only by nature.
subjective.rewrite_language_recommendation: No. Python stdlib is the right fit for a text-slicing CLI that backs a skill.
subjective.merge_recommendation: Keep standalone. It is a reusable CLI with more than one potential consumer; folding it into the skill would lose direct-CLI use.
subjective.rename_recommendation: Optional/low value. Could drop the .py to read as a command, but it is invoked by path from the skill, so renaming buys little.
subjective.relocate_recommendation: Keep in scripts/. It is a general utility, not a rarely-used helper.
subjective.improvement_suggestions: Add a small test suite (pure-function logic, trivially testable — context windows, --between, --last, --count, -F). Optionally stream large files line-by-line instead of reading fully into memory.
subjective.requirements_check_completeness: explicit and complete (argparse validation + clear regex/file error handling); no environment requirements to check.
subjective.external_dependency_breakdown: Scoring policy (v1.0): +1 per env var; +1 per non-standard / separately-installed program (xcrun/simctl, Android SDK tools, maestro, grpcurl, psql, gmtool, node/npm, lnav, etc.); programs shipped with macOS (ps, lsof, top, pgrep, sysctl, open, pbcopy, curl, osascript, system_profiler, git, grep/sed/awk) are NOT counted; +5 if a simulator/emulator is required on the primary path; +10 per large non-default app required (Xcode, Android Studio/SDK, Genymotion, Postgres, brew). Here: env 0 + programs 0 + sim 0 + apps 0 = 0.
subjective.change_score_rationale: Weights (v1.0): Linux portability full-block +8 / partial +4 / portable 0; other dimensions +1 (or +2 where noted). Linux portable 0. Read-whole-file improvement +1. No tests (very testable, backs a skill) +1. Total 2.
subjective.quality_score_rationale: Anchored rubric (v1.0), sub-scores sum to 100 — Error-handling/robustness /25: 17; Tests /20: 0 (no self-tests); Structure/clarity /20: 18; Documentation /15: 13; Portability + explicit requirement checks /20: 20. Total 68. Clean grep-compatible argparse CLI with careful index-bound math and graceful per-file errors; fully portable. Only missing tests and a full-file read.
